assign.outcome:
**`demo.steps()` landed** — a two-column "demo beside its own numbered steps" hero, for pages that used to lead with a title and a paragraph and said too little. No stepwise system existed to revive (checked `ux/Wizard`, `ux/Course`, `core/new/1`'s tutorials — none of them pairs a live demo with steps that mark themselves done); this is new, in `ext/demo` beside `demo()`/`demo.stage()`.

A step is `{ say, when }` — a verb phrase and the DOM event name the demo fires when the reader does the real gesture (`$tree.el.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent("move", { bubbles: true }))` is the whole wiring). A click on the step finishes it too, always. The two-column collapse at a narrow width costs zero new CSS — it rides the `.rail` word Page.css already has.

**Two consumers:**
- [ux/Tree module page](/framework/ux/Tree/) — expand a branch, drag a row above another, turn on Adapt — wired to the tree already on that page.
- [layouts/shell/doc/](/layouts/shell/doc/) — resize the sidebar, pick a design, open the fold — a small self-built stand-in, **not** the live `/layouts/shell/` page itself (why below).
- [ext/demo's own overview](/framework/ext/demo/) now has a live example too, and [the full method doc](/framework/ext/demo/api/steps/).

![ux/Tree at 1280 — the steps hero beside the live tree](ux-tree-1280.png)
![layouts/shell/doc at 1280 — the small stand-in, all three steps done](shell-doc-1280.png)

**What was left, and why:**
- The brief's literal fence named the TOP-LEVEL `layouts/shell/page.js` as the second consumer. I tried it there first, wrapping the real live sidebar+viewport as `demo.steps()`'s own stage. Measured, headless: it breaks that page's own "never scrolls, exactly fills the region" contract — the box `demo.steps()` adds has no height of its own, so `height: 100%` two levels down resolved against nothing and the shell grew to 9,671px of unclipped content instead of ~900px. Fixing it needs a rule in `shell.css`, outside this task's fence. Reverted that file to its original content (plus one comment explaining why, and a pointer to the doc/page.js alternative); built the three gestures as a small stand-in on `layouts/shell/doc/page.js` instead — still literally under `public/layouts/shell/`, ordinary page flow, nothing to fight.
- `demo.steps` is registered by importing `ext/demo/steps.js` as a side effect in each consumer page (the same pattern `layout.js` already uses for `exhibit.js`) rather than centrally in `app.js` — `app.js` is outside this task's fence. A follow-up should add one line there so a future page does not have to remember the import itself.
- The alternative shape the brief asked to record — steps as a rail under a full-width stage, for a demo too wide to fit in the `.rail`'s own column — is written up in [doc/method/steps.md](/framework/ext/demo/api/steps/) but not built; nothing has needed it yet.

Verified headless (Playwright, private server, killed by its real PID after): four pages × 400/1280/1920 = 12 loads, zero console errors on every one; all three named events mark their step done on the real gesture, and the click fallback works identically, on both consumer pages.
